newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-BAGGIO'S MOVE TO PARMA FALLS THROUGH.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BAGGIO'S MOVE TO PARMA FALLS THROUGH.

text.p: AC Milan midfielder Roberto Baggio is still hunting for a club for the new season after a move to European Cup contenders Parma fell through on Friday.
Baggio, who has vowed to leave Milan before the start of next season, had looked certain earlier this week to join last season's serie A runners-up.
"Baggio from Milan to Parma is a deal which is 99 percent concluded," his agent Antonio Caliendo said on Wednesday after meeting officials at Milan.
But on Friday Parma said they were not interested, an announcement which prompted their sporting director Riccardo Sogliano to resign.
Sogliano had been a key figure in the negotiations between Parma, Milan and Baggio, although he stressed the collapse of the deal was not his only reason for quitting.
Italian newspapers reported on Friday that Parma coach Carlo Ancelotti had opposed signing Baggio on tactical grounds.

Just before Parma made their announcement, serie A rivals Udinese revealed they had made an offer for Baggio, once the world's most expensive footballer and still one of the best-known Italian players of his generation.
"Baggio to Udinese? We'd like to, because he's a player who interests us," club sporting director Carlo Piazzolla said.
"Yesterday we made contact with officials from Milan and we said that -- without wanting to interfere with the deal with Parma -- we'd be interested in bringing Baggio to Udine."
Udinese, from the far north-eastern corner of Italy, are a modest club but have qualified for next season's UEFA Cup.

Baggio has always said he would love to play in next year's World Cup finals in France. A move to Udinese could give him the international exposure that he will need to have a chance of getting back into the national side.
